title: Most of an octopus thinks without its brain
topic: Why two thirds of an octopus's neurons sit in its arms rather than its head
voice_script: Two thirds of an octopus is thinking without its brain. Each arm holds its own dense cluster of neurons. The arm tastes what it touches, decides, and acts, before the central brain is involved. Sever one, and it will still reach for food and pass it toward where a mouth used to be. The brain sets the goal. The arms work out the how. It isn't one animal solving a problem. It is nine of them, loosely agreeing.
